rows.wylie: las kyi sgrib pa rnam par dag pa'i mdo las tshogs dang dus ni rnyed gyur nas, zhes bya ba ni ji ltar sa bon mthu ma nyams pa dang ldan pa la sa dang chu dang me, dang rlung dang nam mkha'i rkyen rnams tshogs na dus ji lta ba bzhin du myu gu, mngon par sgrub par byed do
rows.english: The Sutra on the Complete Purification of Every Karmic Obstacle includes that line about "If there comes a situation where they all assemble, and the the time is ripe..." rows.english: In actuality, all these things are completely beyond the realm of possibility; there is no chance that they could have really happened. A being Gone Thus, one who possesses each and every virtuous quality, has eliminated each and every non-virtue; so too have they eliminated the very trace of even the seeds for negativity. rows.acip: 'DI LTAR LEGS PAR BSLABS PA'I SMAN PA BDAG NYID LA NAD MED BZHIN DU YANG NA, BLTAR BSTAN NAS SMAN KHAB DANG TSA BA DAG BSTEN PAR BYAS PAS DE'I RJES SU SLOB PA'I NAD PA DAG YONGS SU SOS PAR BYED PA DE BZHIN DU DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA SMAN PA'I RGYAL PO GNOD PA THAMS CAD ZHI BAR MDZAD PAS KYANG SGRIB PA MI MNGA' NA YANG NGA'I LAS 'DI'O RNAM PAR SMIN PA NI 'DI 'O ZHES PHRIN LAS STON PAR MDZAD DE
rows.wylie: 'di ltar legs par bslabs pa'i sman pa bdag nyid la nad med bzhin du yang na, bltar bstan nas sman khab dang tsha ba dag bsten par byas pas de'i rjes su slob pa'i nad pa dag yongs su sos par byed pa de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa sman pa'i rgyal po gnod pa thams cad zhi bar mdzad pas kyang sgrib pa mi mnga' na yang nga'i las 'di'o rnam par smin pa ni 'di 'o zhes phrin las ston par mdzad de
rows.english: Think of a very well-trained physician; he may not have any kind of illness himself, but still he might let his own blood, or stick himself with a medicine needle, or apply hot steel to himself, just so his students, the sick ones who are following him, will allow him to use these same methods to cure them. The One Gone Thus, the king of all physicians, is the same. Despite the fact that he has put a stop to every harm he himself could ever undergo, and so has no possible obstacle at all, he nonetheless undertakes as one of his enlightened acts to pretend, and to say "this is my karma," and "this is my karma ripening."

rows.english: When we say that a craving spirit looks at a stream of water and sees pus and blood, by the way, we are only talking about some kinds of craving spirits, and not all of them. rows.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

rows.acip: 'O NA RANG LUGS LA SGRIB GNYIS KYI DRI MA SPONG TSUL JI LTAR BYED SNYAM NA BDAG MED, PHRA RAGS GSUM RIM PA BZHIN DU THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA PHAB NAS SGOM BYUNG GIS BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU MTHONG BA NA NYON MONGS PA'I SGRIB PA DANG SHES SGRIB, RAGS PA DANG SHES SGRIB PHRA MO GSUM RTZA BA NAS ZAD PAR BYED NUS ZHES STON PA YIN, PAS DNGOS SMRA BA 'DOD PA LTAR DRI MA BDEN GRUB KHAS BLANGS NAS SPONG BA MIN GYI DRI MA BDEN MED BSGOMS NAS DRI MA SPONG BA YIN NO ZHES RANG LUGS KYI SGRIB GNYIS SPONG TSUL GTZO BOR STON PA YIN
rows.wylie: 'o na rang lugs la sgrib gnyis kyi dri ma spong tshul ji ltar byed snyam na bdag med, phra rags gsum rim pa bzhin du thos bsam gyis gtan la phab nas sgom byung gis bsgoms pas mngon sum du mthong ba na nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang shes sgrib, rags pa dang shes sgrib phra mo gsum rtsa ba nas zad par byed nus zhes ston pa yin, pas dngos smra ba 'dod pa ltar dri ma bden grub khas blangs nas spong ba min gyi dri ma bden med bsgoms nas dri ma spong ba yin no zhes rang lugs kyi sgrib gnyis spong tshul gtso bor ston pa yin
rows.english: "Well then," you may think to yourself, "how do we in our own position describe the process by which one eliminates the various impurities?" It has been taught that: One can gain the ability toput a total end tothe three—that is, to the obstacles of the mental afflictions, to the gross obstacles to omniscience, and to the subtle obstacles to omniscience—if one meditates with that wisdom which grows from meditation and which sees directly the three degrees of the lack of a self-nature; this itself grows from following the practices of study and meditation to come to an understanding of these three. Given this statement, it is not the case that in our own position we believe—as do those who assert the existence of functional things which exist truly—that one can eliminate impurities that one asserts exist in truth. The citation rather is demonstrating the principal tenet of how our own system describes the process of eliminating the two obstacles; that is, that we eliminate impurities by meditating upon how these same impurities lack any true existence. The next selection introduces, briefly, the concept of the three levels of deep practice that correlate to the three degrees of selflessness. It is taken from The "Cloud of Offerings, which Pleases the Wise, and Illuminates the True Thought of the Treatise known as the 'Ornament of Realizations,'" being a Combined Word Commentary and Dialectical Analysis of the Fifth Chapter of the Treatise, by Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748), also an illustrious author of textbooks for Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery (ACIP electronic text S0195, Part Five, ff. 11b-12a).

rows.acip: 'DI LA CHOS RJE RONG tI KA {%tIK} PA DANG, GUNG RU RGYAL MTSAN BZANG PO GNYIS KYIS, STONG NYID KYI DON RTOGS SHING GOMS NA SEMS LA BDEN 'DZIN SGRIB PA MED PAS, STONG PA NYID KYI DON LA SKRAG PA MED DE, PHYIN CI LOG BDEN 'DZIN LAS SHIN TU 'DAS NAS THEG CHEN GYI MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA'I MTHAR THOB PAR BYA BA SANGS RGYAS KYI SAR PHYIN TO ZHES 'CHAD LA,
rows.wylie: 'di la chos rje rong Ti ka {%Tik} pa dang, gung ru rgyal mtshan bzang po gnyis kyis, stong nyid kyi don rtogs shing goms na sems la bden 'dzin sgrib pa med pas, stong pa nyid kyi don la skrag pa med de, phyin ci log bden 'dzin las shin tu 'das nas theg chen gyi mya ngan las 'das pa'i mthar thob par bya ba sangs rgyas kyi sar phyin to zhes 'chad la
rows.english: This part is explained by the Lord of the Teachings, Rongtikpa, and by Gung-ru Gyeltsen Sangpo in the following way: If we come to a realization of this object, emptiness, and then get used to what we have realized, then we no longer possess in our minds the obstacle of believing that things are real. And then because of this, we no longer have any fear about this thing—this emptiness. We go beyond all wrong ways of thinking—beyond all belief in things as real—and then we reach the ultimate end of the process of nirvana: meaning that we attain the level of a Buddha.

rows.acip: 'JAM DBYANGS DGA' BLOS DE NI, GANG DRAN DRAN GYI 'BRU BSNON YIN PAR BSHAD NAS, SA BCU'I NGO SKAL GYI SPANG BYA'I SGRIB PA GNYIS GNYIS YOD PA RNAMS RIM GYIS SPANGS TE, PHYIN CI LOG BZHIS 'JIGS SKRAGS PA MED PAS, DE LAS 'DAS PA'I MI GNAS PA'I MYANG 'DAS THOB PAR 'CHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: 'jam dbyangs dga' blos de ni, gang dran dran gyi 'bru bsnon yin par bshad nas, sa bcu'i ngo skal gyi spang bya'i sgrib pa gnyis gnyis yod pa rnams rim gyis spangs te, phyin ci log bzhis 'jigs skrags pa med pas, de las 'das pa'i mi gnas pa'i myang 'das thob par 'chad do
rows.english: Jamyang Gaway Lodru expresses the opinion that this particular section is a spontaneous attachment to the thoughts already expressed. He explains that there are pairs of obstacles that are eliminated specifically at the tenth bodhisattva level, and that these are eliminated in stages. And then with this, we are freed of the terror of the four backwards thoughts. And as we pass beyond that stage, we attain the nirvana where nothing remains.

rows.acip: SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI SEMS BDEN PAS STONG PA'I CHOS NYID DE LA SGRIB PA RIM GYIS SBYANGS TE MTHAR SGRIB PA MTHA' DAG ZAD NAS SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS SKUR GYUR PA NI DPE DE'I DON NO ZHES BYAS NA DGONGS PAR 'GRO'AM SNYAM MO,,

rows.english: The minds of all living beings have an obstacle which prevents them from seeing the actual nature of things—where things are empty of any true existence. This then catches the point of the illustration.

rows.english: (25) The secondary offense of failing to purge yourself of the obstacles to meditation Suppose you have any one or combination of the five typical obstacles to meditation: the pair of restless desire and missing something or someone; feelings of malice about someone; the pair of drowsiness and mental dullness; attraction to the objects of the senses; and unresolved doubts. You commit this offense when you allow yourself these five, and fail to act to dispel them.

rows.english: (37) The secondary offense of failing to remove suffering Suppose a person is suffering due to any one or combination of the following seven problems: they are blind, deaf, handicapped, weary from travelling, tormented by any of the five mental obstacles, haunted by thoughts such as malice towards someone, or suffering from defeat at the hands of someone else. You commit this offense if, out of anger or laziness, you fail to make some attempt to remove the suffering they are undergoing due to the problem they have. rows.acip: THUN MONG MA YIN PA GANG SNANG KUN BDE STONG DBYER MED DU 'CHAR BA LA SGRIB PA'I DRI MA 'KHRUD PAS YID DAG PAR BYED, 'OD GSAL PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO BSGOM PA LA DBANG BAR BYAS, 'BRAS BU CHOS KYI SKU MNGON DU GYUR BA'I NUS PA KHYAD PAR CAN 'JOG GO ,

rows.english: The unique result of this initiation is that it purifies your mind, cleaning it of a special impurity: your tendency to be blinded to the fact that every single thing which ever appears to you is a manifestation of indivisible bliss and empitness. Finally, an extraordinary seed has been planted within you which gives you the power to attain the final goal of the Dharma body.

rows.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR THABS DANG SHES RAB DBYER MED PAR SBYOR BA'I RDO RJE SEMS DPA'I RNAL 'BYOR NI RDO RJE STE THEG PA YANG DE'O, ,DE LA 'DIS 'GRO BA RGYU'I THEG PA DANG 'DIR 'GRO BA 'BRAS BU'I THEG PA GNYIS SO, ,THEG PA DES 'GRO BA'I SNGAGS KYI SDOM LDAN RNAMS LA BCAS PA'I BCAS PA DANG 'GAL BA'I LAS KYI SGRIB PA NI GNAS 'OG MAR 'KHRID PA DANG , YON TAN GONG MA SKYE BA LA SGRIB PAS NA LTUNG BA YIN LA,
rows.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar thabs dang shes rab dbyer med par sbyor ba'i rdo rje sems dpa'i rnal 'byor ni rdo rje ste theg pa yang de'o, ,de la 'dis 'gro ba rgyu'i theg pa dang 'dir 'gro ba 'bras bu'i theg pa gnyis so, ,theg pa des 'gro ba'i sngags kyi sdom ldan rnams la bcas pa'i bcas pa dang 'gal ba'i las kyi sgrib pa ni gnas 'og mar 'khrid pa dang , yon tan gong ma skye ba la sgrib pas na ltung ba yin la
rows.english: What Shantipa is describing here is that the yoga of the Warrior of Diamond is where we yoke together, indivisibly, method and wisdom.  This then is both the diamond and the way. This diamond way is both a way which is a cause--that is, a way by which we make our spiritual journey; and a way which is a result--the place to which we are journeying. Now when those who are traveling upon this way--that is, those who possess the vows of the secret word--act against the rules that have been set down for them, then this creates a karmic obstacle.  This obstacle leads them to a lower place, and obstructs them from developing higher spiritual qualities.  As such, it is called a "downfall."

rows.acip: CI LU PA'I 'DUS KYI 'GREL PA LAS, RNAM PA GNYIS SU DBYER MA MCHIS SO, ,ZHES PA NI BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS RDO RJE'I CHOS KYI SKU LAS LONGS SPYOD RDZOGS PA 'BYUNG ZHING DE NYID KYI SPRUL PA'I GZUGS RNAM PAR GNAS PA MTHONG BA'I LAM DU MI 'GYUR BA'I DUS SU DE'I LUS LA RNAM PAR GNAS NAS GZHAN GYI LAS KYI SGRIB PA LA SOGS SBYONG BAR BYED PAS NA'O, ,ZHES SANGS RGYAS DNGOS SU MTHONG MI NUS PA DA LTA 'DRA BA'I DUS SU SANGS RGYAS RNAMS RDO RJE SLOB DPON GYI LUS LA BZHUGS NAS SEMS CAN GYI DON MDZAD PAR GSUNGS SO,
rows.wylie: ci lu pa'i 'dus kyi 'grel pa las, rnam pa gnyis su dbyer ma mchis so, ,zhes pa ni byang chub kyi sems rdo rje'i chos kyi sku las longs spyod rdzogs pa 'byung zhing de nyid kyi sprul pa'i gzugs rnam par gnas pa mthong ba'i lam du mi 'gyur ba'i dus su de'i lus la rnam par gnas nas gzhan gyi las kyi sgrib pa la sogs sbyong bar byed pas na'o, ,zhes sangs rgyas dngos su mthong mi nus pa da lta 'dra ba'i dus su sangs rgyas rnams rdo rje slob dpon gyi lus la bzhugs nas sems can gyi don mdzad par gsungs so
rows.english: Chilupa's commentary to the Secret Collection says too that "They are completely indivisible."   What this is saying is that the paradise body of the being known as the Diamond Mind of Enlightenment arises from his Dharma body.  We live though in times where we are unable even to lay eyes upon the bodies of emanation in which these other bodies reside. And so the Enlightened Ones come and stay in the body of our Master, so that they can help others purify themselves of their karmic obstacles, and other such problems. The point is that in times like the present day, when people are unable to see a Buddha in the flesh, then the Enlightened Ones come and enter into the body of our Diamond Master, and thus perform Their deeds of benefit for every living being. ***

rows.acip: RKANG PA DANG PO GNYIS NI SMON 'JUG GNYIS KYI DON BSDU DANG , DE NAS GNYIS NI SDOM PA LNGA'I DON BSDU'O, ,MA GROL PA NI GTI MUG SOGS SGRIB PA GNYIS KYI 'CHING BAS BCINGS PA'I TSANGS PA LA SOGS PA STE DE RNAMS DGROL BA DANG NYAN RANG SHES SGRIB LAS MA BRGAL BA RNAMS DE LAS BSGRAL BA DANG , DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA DBUGS MA PHYIN PA RNAMS DBUGS DBYUNG ZHING SEMS CAN KUN MI GNAS PA'I MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA LA DGOD DO ZHES PA NI MAN SNYE DANG RDO RJE MKHA' 'GRO'I RNAM BSHAD GNYIS KA'I DGONGS PA'O, ,TSIGS BCAD THA MA 'DI 'JUG SEMS BSKYED PA LA MAN SNYER BSHAD DO,
rows.wylie: rkang pa dang po gnyis ni smon 'jug gnyis kyi don bsdu dang , de nas gnyis ni sdom pa lnga'i don bsdu'o, ,ma grol pa ni gti mug sogs sgrib pa gnyis kyi 'ching bas bcings pa'i tshangs pa la sogs pa ste de rnams dgrol ba dang nyan rang shes sgrib las ma brgal ba rnams de las bsgral ba dang , dmyal ba la sogs pa dbugs ma phyin pa rnams dbugs dbyung zhing sems can kun mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa la dgod do zhes pa ni man snye dang rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i rnam bshad gnyis ka'i dgongs pa'o, ,tshigs bcad tha ma 'di 'jug sems bskyed pa la man snyer bshad do
rows.english: The first four lines [in the English] here summarize the meaning of the Wish for enlightenment, in both the form of a prayer, and action.  The next two lines summarize the five vows. The words "those who have yet to be freed" refer to beings such as the Pure One, Brahma, who are still bound in the fetters of ignorance and so on: the two kinds of obstacles; and we commit to free them. "Those who have yet to be saved" refers to those of the ways of listeners and self-made Buddhas, who are yet to be saved from the obstacles to omniscience; we commit to save them. "Those who have no comfort" is a reference to beings such as those in the realms of hell; we are resolving to bring them comfort.  And we decide finally to deliver all living beings to a state of nirvana which is beyond both of the extremes.  This is how both the Golden Harvest and the Explication of the Angel of Diamond both interpret these lines.  The Golden Harvest further explains the final verse as referring to the Wish for enlightenment in the form of action. ***

rows.english: In this system, all our spiritual obstacles are subsumed within the obstacles relating to these four types of drops.  The drops then are said to be the expression of these obstacles.  What this means is that the extremely subtle winds and thoughts which reside in these drops provide the foundation which is infected with the mental seeds of the obstacles.

rows.wylie: da ltar rang res bla ma mi'i gzugs can du mthong ba yang dga' rab yin te, spyan snga blo rgyan gyis, ,rang re'i las ngan sgrib pa'i che tshod la, ,bla ma mi ru mthong ba'ang dga' tshad yin, ,khyi dang bong bur ma mthong bsod nams che, ,mos gus snying nas bskyed cig shAkya'i sras, ,zhes gsungs
rows.english: Even the fact that we can in our present condition see our Lama as a human being is quite an achievement.  As Chen-nga Lodru Gyeltsen once said, The fact that all of us, with the level Of bad deeds and obstacles that we have, Can even see our Lama as a human Is quite something of an achievement. It is our own great merit that we don't See Them as a dog, or a donkey. So feel love and reverence for Them, Deep from your hearts, Sons of the Shakya.

rows.acip: BLA MA'I SPYI BO'I AOm LAS BDUD RTZI DKAR PO'I RGYUN BABS RANG GI SPYI BOR THIM, BUM PA'I DBANG THOB, LUS KYI SGRIB PA DAG ,LAM BSKYED RIM BSGOM PA LA DBANG, 'BRAS BU SPRUL SKU 'GRUB PA'I NUS PA BZHAG
rows.wylie: bla ma'i spyi bo'i aoM las bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun babs rang gi spyi bor thim, bum pa'i dbang thob, lus kyi sgrib pa dag ,lam bskyed rim bsgom pa la dbang, 'bras bu sprul sku 'grub pa'i nus pa bzhag
rows.english: From the letter om at the tips of the Lamas' heads comes forth a stream of white nectar.  It dissolves into the tip of your own head.  You receive the empowerment of the vase, and you are purified of all your physical obstacles.  You are empowered to practice the path of the stage of creation, and the ability to achieve one of your goals--the Emanation Body--is planted within you.

rows.english: The gods of the Thirty-Three, and the Four Great Kings, do experience the bliss of joining the two organs, but as nothing more than the pleasure of the joining and mixing of the winds.  They do not get the experience of bliss that comes from channels, and the red and white elements, because they do not possess any of these inner parts.  Craving spirits and animals do possess the pleasure of union of the organs, but they have very bad obstacles caused by their past karma and are spiritually very stupid, and thus they are incapable of making this bliss a path.

rows.acip: 'KHOR LO SNGA MA LTAR NA PHYI NANG GNYIS KYI RTZIBS BCU DRUG ,RANG LUGS THUN MONG MIN PAR 'KHOR LO'I RTZIBS BRGYAD DANG NOR BU'I GZHOGS KHA BRGYAD BSDOMS PAS BCU DRUG ,RDO RJE NAG PO'I PHRENG BA PHYI NANG GNYIS BSDOMS PA BCU DRUG STE KHYON SUM CU SO GNYIS KYIS SPYI BO'I RTZA 'DAB SUM CU SO GNYIS MTSON, 'KHOR LOS DBU SKRA MI SGRIB PA DANG, DBU SKRAS 'KHOR LO MI SGRIB PAR BSGOM DGOS,
rows.wylie: 'khor lo snga ma ltar na phyi nang gnyis kyi rtsibs bcu drug ,rang lugs thun mong min par 'khor lo'i rtsibs brgyad dang nor bu'i gzhogs kha brgyad bsdoms pas bcu drug ,rdo rje nag po'i phreng ba phyi nang gnyis bsdoms pa bcu drug ste khyon sum cu so gnyis kyis spyi bo'i rtsa 'dab sum cu so gnyis mtshon, 'khor los dbu skra mi sgrib pa dang, dbu skras 'khor lo mi sgrib par bsgom dgos
rows.english: Each spoke of the circular headdress, as we spoke of above, has an inner and outer section, totaling then 16 pieces.  In our own system though we have a unique way of arriving at this number 16, by adding together the eight spokes of the wheel and the eight facets of the jewels at the top.  We then add another 16 for the two strings of black diamonds, inside and out, which brings us to a total of 32.  This represents the 32 petals of the chakra at the center tip of the head.  In your meditation don't let the headdress block Her hair, nor Her hair block the headdress.

rows.english: These lines describe how, in the short run, all of the obstacles caused by one's past deeds are purified. To be more specific, they win a rebirth as one of the Wheel Empowered Emperors of the World.

rows.acip: DE YANG TSOGS GSOG PAR 'DOD NA YAR NGO DANG, SGRIB PA SBYONG BA 'DOD NA MAR NGO ZHES GANG RUNG GCIG GIS CHOG PA 'DRA ZHIG 'DUG KYANG GNYIS KA MA CHAG PA NI GAL CHE'O,,
rows.wylie: de yang tshogs gsog par 'dod na yar ngo dang, sgrib pa sbyong ba 'dod na mar ngo zhes gang rung gcig gis chog pa 'dra zhig 'dug kyang gnyis ka ma chag pa ni gal che'o
rows.english: Now it has been said, correctly, that if you're looking to collect new good karma you can do so powerfully during the Offering of the Tenth that falls during the waxing of the moon; and that if you hope to remove old bad karma it is well done on the Tenth during the moon's waning.  This would seem to imply that you could observe either one of these two; but in truth you should be aware that it's extremely important never to break your observance of both tenth days. The Yoga of Offering Torma Cakes

rows.acip: YI GE GSUM NI RDO RJE GSUM GYI MTSON BYED YIN LA, DE GSUM GYIS SGRIB PA GSUM SBYONG BA BZHIN DU, DBANG GSUM GYIS KYANG SBYONG BA 'DRA BA TZAM DANG, DON GYI DBANG BZHI PA RDO RJE GSUM DBYER MI PHYED PAS PHRA BA'I SGRIB PA SBYONG BA LA BSAMS NAS, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I DBANG BZHI THOB PA'I THA SNYAD BYAS PA TZAM YIN GYI, DES DBANG DNGOS THOB PA MIN NO,,
rows.wylie: yi ge gsum ni rdo rje gsum gyi mtshon byed yin la, de gsum gyis sgrib pa gsum sbyong ba bzhin du, dbang gsum gyis kyang sbyong ba 'dra ba tsam dang, don gyi dbang bzhi pa rdo rje gsum dbyer mi phyed pas phra ba'i sgrib pa sbyong ba la bsams nas, sngar bshad pa'i dbang bzhi thob pa'i tha snyad byas pa tsam yin gyi, des dbang dngos thob pa min no
rows.english: The three syllables symbolize the three diamonds; these three purify you of the three obstacles.  The "three empowerments" here are similar, merely representing the same purification.  The ultimate empowerment, the fourth, is where the three diamonds, inseparable, have cleaned you of even your most subtle obstacles.  This is all that is meant when it is stated above that you "receive the four empowerments"; it's not though that by visualizing it you have actually been granted the empowerments themselves.

rows.acip: DES NA STONG NYID KYI DON GTAN LA 'BABS TSUL KHYAD MED KYANG DE'I DON SGOM PAR BYED PA NA, GA-YAS GA-YON GYI RLUNG DH'U T'IR BTZUD NAS DER THIM PA'I DBANG GIS GTUM MO 'BAR BAS BYANG SEMS BZHUS PA'I BDE BA CHEN POS STONG PA'I DON NGES NAS SGOM PA'I LHAN SKYES KYIS SGRIB PA'I BAG CHAGS SBYONG MYUR BA'I NUS PA 'DRA BA YUL CAN GZHAN GANG LA'ANG MED PAS, NGES PAR BDE BA DE BSKYED DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: des na stong nyid kyi don gtan la 'babs tshul khyad med kyang de'i don sgom par byed pa na, ga-yas ga-yon gyi rlung dhU tIr btsud nas der thim pa'i dbang gis gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems bzhus pa'i bde ba chen pos stong pa'i don nges nas sgom pa'i lhan skyes kyis sgrib pa'i bag chags sbyong myur ba'i nus pa 'dra ba yul can gzhan gang la'ang med pas, nges par bde ba de bskyed dgos so
rows.english: We can say thus that there is no difference between the open and secret teachings on the question of how we establish the fact that everything is empty.  When in the secret teachings we perform a meditation upon this fact, we utilize a feeling of great bliss--bliss which arises when we are able to get the right and left winds into the channel of dance, and dissolve there.  This brings the inner fire to blaze, which melts down the element of enlightenment, bringing on then the great bliss. We use this bliss to perceive the fact that things are empty of themselves.  This simultaneous bliss and voidness, as we meditate with it, has the capacity to rid us quickly of all the propensities we have within us for spiritual obstacles.  There is no other subject state of mind which can compare with this one--combined bliss and emptiness--and so the case is that we absolutely must reach this state of bliss.

rows.acip: DE LTAR SDIG PA THAMS CAD LAS RNAM PAR GROL BAR BYED CING, LUS TE RGYUD DAG PA LAS SKYON MED PA'I MI'I MCHOG KUN NAS GTZANG SBRA'I SPYOD PA BYED PA DE, SDIG PA STE SGRIB PA THAMS CAD RNAM PAR DAG PA'I DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RDO RJE 'CHANG GI SA 'THOB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: de ltar sdig pa thams cad las rnam par grol bar byed cing, lus te rgyud dag pa las skyon med pa'i mi'i mchog kun nas gtsang sbra'i spyod pa byed pa de, sdig pa ste sgrib pa thams cad rnam par dag pa'i de bzhin gshegs pa rdo rje 'chang gi sa 'thob par 'gyur ro
rows.english: They too are, in the same way, liberated from all their own bad deeds; their body--which is to say, their mindstream--becomes completely pure.  They then become the immaculate Lord of All Beings, engaging in His own form of purity.  That is, they achieve the state of the One Gone Thus, the Keeper of the Diamond, free of every "bad deed," here meaning "obstacle." * * * On the need for an actual, physical partner, Choney Lama (writing in the 17th century) mentions a disagreement on the matter and expresses his own opinion in the Lamp that Illuminates the Essence: An Explanation of Critical Points in the "Harvest of Attainments" [of Je Tsongkapa], itself a Treatise on the Great, Deep Practice of the Stage of Completion, according to the System of that Great and Accomplished Saint, Luhipa (ACIP digital text S00299, ff. 35b-36a):

rows.english: One may continue with the following objection: "If something is a mental affliction, then it's necessarily an obstacle to spiritual progress. And in this case it would be a contradiction to say it were a cause for this enlightenment."

rows.acip: SUM CU RTZA GSUM DANG RGYAL CHEN RIGS BZHI'I LHA RNAMS LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYANG RLUNG 'DU 'PHROD KYI BDE BA TZAM LAS RTZA DANG KHAMS DKAR DMAR MED PAS DE'I BDE BA MED, YI DVAGS DANG DUD 'GRO LA DBANG PO GNYIS SBYOR GYI BDE BA YOD KYKANG LAS KYI SGRIB PA CHE ZHING DBANG PO RTUL BAS BDE BA LAM DU BYED MI NUS LA,
rows.wylie: sum cu rtsa gsum dang rgyal chen rigs bzhi'i lha rnams la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kyang rlung 'du 'phrod kyi bde ba tsam las rtsa dang khams dkar dmar med pas de'i bde ba med, yi dvags dang dud 'gro la dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi bde ba yod kykang las kyi sgrib pa che zhing dbang po rtul bas bde ba lam du byed mi nus la
rows.english: The gods of the Thirty-Three, and the Four Great Kings, do experience the bliss of joining the two organs, but as nothing more than the pleasure of the joining and mixing of the winds.  They do not get the experience of bliss that comes from channels, and the red and white elements, because they do not possess any of these inner parts.  Craving spirits and animals do possess the pleasure of union of the organs, but they have very bad obstacles caused by their past karma and are spiritually very stupid, and thus they are incapable of making this bliss a path.

rows.acip: GNYIS PA YAN LAG BDUN PO DE BSAGS SBYANG SPEL GSUM DU 'DU BAR BSTAN PA NI, PHYAG DANG MCHOD PA YI RANG DANG BSKUL BA DANG GSOL 'DEBS LNGA NI, TSOGS GSOGS PA'I YAN LAG ,BSHAGS PA NI SGRIB PA SBYONG BA'I YAN LAG, BSNGO BA NI DGE BA MI ZAD CING GONG 'PHEL DU BYED PA'I YAN LAG GO , (,ZHES YAN LAG BDUN PA 'BUL ZHING, LONG BYUNG TSE, BSHAGS PA'I MTSAMS SU SDOM PA GSUM SO SO'I BSHAGS PA DANG, BLA MA RDOR 'DZIN MA DANG, BYANG CHUB LTUNG BSHAGS SOGS BYA'O,,)
rows.wylie: gnyis pa yan lag bdun po de bsags sbyang spel gsum du 'du bar bstan pa ni, phyag dang mchod pa yi rang dang bskul ba dang gsol 'debs lnga ni, tshogs gsogs pa'i yan lag ,bshags pa ni sgrib pa sbyong ba'i yan lag, bsngo ba ni dge ba mi zad cing gong 'phel du byed pa'i yan lag go , (,zhes yan lag bdun pa 'bul zhing, long byung tshe, bshags pa'i mtshams su sdom pa gsum so so'i bshags pa dang, bla ma rdor 'dzin ma dang, byang chub ltung bshags sogs bya'o,,)
rows.english: This brings us back to our original second point, which is the presentation of a summary of everything into the three points of collecting good deeds; clearing ourselves of obstacles; and increasing the power.  Now the five steps of bowing down to our Lama, making Them offerings, rejoicing in the goodness of all, entreating our Lama to teach, and supplicating Them to stay can all be considered steps where we are collecting good deeds--good karma.  The step of confession is one where we clear ourselves of obstacles.  And then the step of dedication is one where we assure that our good deeds will never wear out, but rather grow ever higher.  Practice thus the Seven Steps.  At the point where you offer your confession, you can--if time permits--confess transgressions of any of the individual vows found in the three sets of commitments; recite the Prayer of the Lama, the Keeper of the Diamond; and go through the Confession of the Downfalls of a Bodhisattva, or other similar practices.

rows.acip: DE NYID NGO BO JI LTA BU ZHE NA, (SGRIB MED) STE SGRIB PA DANG BRAL BA'I (LHAN SKYES) KYI (DGA' BA'I) NGO BOR GYUR PA'I YE SHES KYI RNAM PAR (ROL BA DANG) NGO BO (DBYER MED) PA'I CHOS KYI DBYINGS STONG PA NYID DE,

rows.acip: DE NAS (CIG CHAR) DU (BYUNG NAS) DE RNAMS RIM PA BZHIN DU SGRUB PA PO (BDAG NYID KYI) SPYI BO MGRIN PA SNYING GA'I (GNAS GSUM) DU SNGA PHYI (RIM) CHAR (DANG,) DE NAS (CIG CHAR) DU (THIM PA) NAS THUN MONG BA LTAR NA SROG GCOD SOGS LUS KYI SGRIB PA DANG, RDZUN DU SMRA BA SOGS NGAG GI SGRIB PA DANG, BRNAB SEMS SOGS YID KYI SGRIB PA DANG, SGO GSUM THUN MONG GI SGRIB PA STE (SGRIB) PA (BZHI DAG CING,)
rows.wylie: de nas (cig char) du (byung nas) de rnams rim pa bzhin du sgrub pa po (bdag nyid kyi) spyi bo mgrin pa snying ga'i (gnas gsum) du snga phyi (rim) char (dang,) de nas (cig char) du (thim pa) nas thun mong ba ltar na srog gcod sogs lus kyi sgrib pa dang, rdzun du smra ba sogs ngag gi sgrib pa dang, brnab sems sogs yid kyi sgrib pa dang, sgo gsum thun mong gi sgrib pa ste (sgrib) pa (bzhi dag cing,)
rows.english: And then they come as one, sinking into my body; into the same three places on me, the practitioner; that is, into the tip of the head, the throat, and the heart.  First they come one after the other, and then they come as one.  Relative to the shared teachings, these rays of light clean us of the four kinds of obstacles: obstacles relating to our actions (deeds such as the taking of life); obstacles relating to our speech (things like telling lies); and obstacles relating to our thoughts (such as being unhappy when others get something)--along with obstacles that involve all three of these doors of expression.
